subject: MAP & evaluation plan: overage/burst rates and ramp caps for Acme IoT
messages:
From: Tom Barnes <tbarnes@acme-iot.com>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acme-iot.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: MAP & burst pricing questions for eval

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the demo last week — the latency numbers look promising. We're lining up an internal eval and need to lock down a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and the commercial guardrails for the ramp. Two quick asks from our side before we commit to dates:

1) During the 60-day ramp/eval, what are the explicit caps on burst/overage pricing? We expect spikes during ingestion tests and we'd like a clear cap so our finance team can model worst-case costs.

2) If we hit key milestones in the MAP early (e.g., throughput >= 95% target by day 30), is there an associated discount or credit that we can apply retroactively?

3) Can you confirm the rate card that will be used for the evaluation (committed vs burst rates) and whether we can pin rates for the duration of the eval?

Procurement is copied and will want the draft SOW and ratecard. Target goal: start eval week of Mar 8 and close by Mar 26 if all goes well.

Thanks,
Tom Barnes
Head of AI Platform
Acme IoT

--

Tom — really appreciate the clear asks. Quick answers at a glance, and I'll follow up with a formal MAP and SOW PDF attached: redwood-map-draft.pdf and the current ratecard (ratecard-v3.xlsx).

- Short answer on caps: We can set an explicit burst cap for the eval period. Proposal: burst billed at the published burst rate, but with a cap of 200% of the committed monthly usage for months 1-2 (see details in attached). After month 3 the cap relaxes to standard overage terms.
- Milestone credits: We can structure a milestone credit for early delivery of throughput targets: if throughput >= 95% for two consecutive weeks within the first 30 days, we can apply a one-time credit equivalent to 5% of that month's usage invoice.
- Rate card: ratecard-v3.xlsx attached. We'll lock the rates for the 60-day eval window as long as the MAP is signed prior to the start date.

I'll loop in Rishi and Lauren internally to confirm pricing and approvals; they can help finalize the exact caps and commit amounts.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 10:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Acme MAP questions — need quick pricing alignment

FW: see below — Acme is asking for a hard cap and a milestone credit. Tom wants to start the eval week of Mar 8, close by Mar 26. Procurement wants a SOW and pinned ratecard.

My suggested structure (high level):
- Committed baseline: 200k tokens/month for 3 months (commit covers months 1-3), with a 3-month minimum term tied to the eval.
- Committed rate: $0.035 / 1K tokens (applies to committed baseline usage).
- Burst rate during eval: $0.12 / 1K tokens, but capped to 200% of committed usage for months 1-2. For month 3, standard overage rules (no cap).
- Milestone credit: 5% back of the invoice for the month they meet throughput >=95% for 2 consecutive weeks within first 30 days.
- Early termination: standard SOW termination language with 30-day notice; no retroactive credits beyond the milestone credit above.

Questions for Rishi / Lauren: are the numbers above (commit + rate + burst cap) workable from finance/ops perspective? Also need to confirm we can guarantee the cap in the contract (legal will weigh in but want your quick take).

Thanks — need to get a formal MAP to Acme by Friday EOD so they can run procurement review.

--
Jasmine
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 08:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Acme MAP questions — need quick pricing alignment

Thanks for the layout, Jaz. Finance/Commercial reviewed and we can support the structure with a couple of clarifications and one tightening ask from Legal:

1) Commit and ramp: 200k tokens/month is fine as the committed baseline. We should set an explicit ramp schedule in the MAP:
   - Week 1-2: proof-of-concept ingestion, expected 40-60k tokens/week.
   - Week 3-6: targeted ramp to 200k tokens/month.
   - Weeks 7-12: steady-state at or above committed baseline.

2) Burst cap & billing: we can commit to the 200% cap for months 1-2 (billing at burst rate $0.12 / 1K tokens). Important: cap must be an invoicing cap (i.e., we won't bill above the cap amount) but operationally we will still serve requests above the cap — those will be queued or throttled based on SLO. Legal wants a clause that allows us to temporarily throttle if the customer's spikes impact system stability.

3) Milestone credit: 5% credit is acceptable but tie it to a measured metric (95% of 99th-percentile throughput target) and require both sides to sign off on the evaluation test harness results.

4) Contract mechanics: agree to pin rates for the 60-day eval window. After the eval, standard renewal pricing applies.

5) Redlines: Legal asks that the cap period be explicit (e.g., Feb 1 - Mar 31 for eval) — we should not leave open-ended language.

If that sounds good, Lauren can bake these into the MAP PDF, and Jasmine can send to Acme.

-Rishi
VP, Commercial Operations

Subject: Draft MAP, SOW & ratecard — Acme eval window Mar 8 - May 7

Tom — attaching the formal MAP/SOW and the ratecard (redwood-map-draft.pdf, SOW-acme.docx, ratecard-v3.xlsx). Key commercial points summarized below for quick review:

1) Eval window: Mar 8 - May 7 (60 days). MAP must be signed by Mar 5 to lock rates.
2) Commit: 200k tokens/month (months 1-3) at $0.035 / 1K tokens.
3) Burst: billed at $0.12 / 1K tokens; invoicing cap at 200% of committed monthly usage for months 1-2. Operationally we may throttle requests that materially affect cluster stability; threshold/threshold handling described in section 4.2 of the SOW.
4) Milestone credit: 5% credit on the month invoice if throughput >=95% of the 99th-percentile target for two consecutive weeks within the first 30 days; both parties sign off on test harness report to unlock credit.
4) Rates locked for the evaluation period; after the eval the standard renewal ratecard applies unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.

Next steps: If this aligns, Procurement can issue a PO referencing DEAL-2026-0842 and we will prepare a final contract for signature. Our target close date per your earlier note: Mar 26 (but we can accelerate if Procurement sends the PO/contract redlines sooner).

Thanks and happy to hop on a 20-min call if Procurement has detailed questions.

Best,
Jasmine Liu

If you accept the month-1 cap, Procurement is prepared to issue a PO next week and Legal will send minor redlines. We aim to kick off Mar 8 as planned.
